transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um... hi. I guess... well, I'm having a hard time lately with, um, my face. The left side of it. It just looks really uneven and... puffy. 

I can't really stop focusing on it, especially when I have to be on video calls for work, or... if I see photos of myself from my salsa class. Everyone keeps telling me they don't see anything, but... I don't know. It's just starting to really mess with my job, and my social life, I guess. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Do you find yourself checking your face in mirrors or other reflective surfaces often, or trying to fix or hide the left side of your face in any way?

Um... yeah, I guess so. I mean... before I log into a meeting, or if I'm supposed to go somewhere, I... I tend to open the camera preview a lot. Just to check. I end up changing the angle, or messing with the lighting... and I try to fix my hair so it falls over that side of my face to hide it. 

Sometimes I take pictures to see how it looks, and I just keep retaking them. I ask my friends if I look strange, but... I don't know. It takes up a lot of time. Half the time I end up being late, or... I just get so drained from doing all that, I don't even want to go out anymore.
Do you feel distressed or anxious about the way your face looks, to the point where it's hard to control those thoughts or the things you do to try to fix or check your appearance?
Yeah... I guess so. It's... it's really stressful. I try not to think about it, but... the thoughts just kind of stay there. And... I don't know, I just can't seem to stop checking. It's hard.

When you look at your face and notice the unevenness, do you feel certain that something is physically wrong or changed, even if others don't see it, or does it come and go depending on how you're feeling at the moment?
Um... I don't know. I guess... I just see it. It's just there. I don't really know if it changes or not. I just... I know what I see.
Do you believe that the unevenness on your face is due to an actual physical defect, or is it more of a feeling or sense that something is off without being sure it's visible to others?
I mean... it's just there. It's not just a feeling. I look in the mirror and... I can see it. It's physical. Even if people say they don't notice, I know what I'm looking at.
Would you say that your concern about the left side of your face is more about a specific physical feature you believe is defective, or is it more about how you feel about your appearance overall?

I think it's... a specific thing. It's just that the left side looks uneven and... puffy. I just can't stop focusing on it when I have to be on video calls for work, or... if I see photos of myself from salsa dancing. Everyone keeps telling me they don't see anything, but... I do. And it's... it's just starting to really mess with my work and my social life.
When you're worried about the left side of your face, do you find yourself doing specific mental exercises, counting, or trying to control your thoughts in a particular way to reduce the anxiety?
Um... no. I don't really do anything like that. No counting or... mental exercises. I just... worry about it, I guess.

When you're feeling anxious about the left side of your face, do you find yourself repeating certain behaviors — like checking your face, adjusting your hair, or taking multiple photos — in a specific way to try to feel better or reduce your worry?

I guess so. Before work meetings or... if I'm supposed to go out... I just, I have to open the camera on my phone first. I check the preview. I try to change the lighting, or the angle, just to see how bad it is. And I mess with my hair... trying to cover that side of my face. Sometimes I take a bunch of pictures to check. Or I ask my friends if I look weird. I just keep doing it until... I don't know, until I'm late for whatever I'm supposed to be doing, or I'm just too tired to even go.
How much time per day would you say you spend thinking about or dealing with your concern about the left side of your face?
I don't really know... I've never timed it. I guess it's just... a lot. I don't have an exact number of hours or anything.
Do you feel that you have to perform certain actions or rituals a specific number of times or in a certain way when you’re checking your face or adjusting your hair to feel reassured?
Um... no. Not really. I don't have a specific number of times or... a routine or anything like that. I don't count. I just... do it. Like I said, I just keep checking until I have to leave.
Have you ever felt that this facial unevenness makes you look unattractive or deformed in a way that others should notice, even if they don’t seem to?

Yeah... I mean, to me, it's really obvious. The left side just looks so uneven and... puffy. Especially if I have to be on a video call for work, or in photos from my salsa class. I think it looks terrible. 

But... everyone keeps telling me they don't see anything at all. I don't really get how they wouldn't notice. It's kind of why I came in, honestly. It's just... it's starting to really mess with my job and my social life.
Does this concern about the left side of your face cause you significant distress or interfere with your ability to function normally in your daily life, such as at work or in social situations?

Yeah... um. Like I said, it's affecting things. At work, I've... I've missed a few ticket deadlines. And I've joined some of those video calls late because I just... I couldn't get past how I looked. My supervisor actually brought it up in my last performance review. 

And... socially, I've just been skipping things. Like salsa nights, or community events. Just... if I know people are going to be taking photos, I'd rather just not go.

Do you feel driven to perform any specific behaviors or mental acts in response to the thoughts about your face, such as checking, adjusting, or reassurance-seeking, because you feel that something bad might happen if you don’t?

Um... I don't know about thinking something bad will happen. But... yeah, I do those things. 

Like, before a meeting, or if I'm supposed to go out... I'll open the camera preview. I just... keep changing the angle, or the lighting. I try to fix my hair around that side of my face. I'll retake pictures to see how it looks... and ask my friends if I look strange. I just kind of keep doing it until I'm late. Or... until I'm just too drained to actually go.

Do you find that your concern about the left side of your face feels different from other worries you’ve had in your life — like it’s more of a physical certainty rather than just a fear or anxious thought?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't... I haven't really thought about it like that. It's just... what I see when I look at it. I don't know if it feels different from other things.
Do you feel like you have to do certain things—like checking your face, adjusting your hair, or taking pictures—over and over again, even if you know it might not make sense?

Yeah... I mean, I guess I just said that. I... I do those things. 

Like I mentioned, before a meeting or going out, I'll... open the camera. I keep checking the preview, moving the light around, trying to cover that side with my hair. I take pictures over and over. I ask people if it looks weird. I just... I keep doing it. Even if I know I'm going to be late. Or until I just... give up and don't go.

Do you believe that the unevenness on the left side of your face is something that makes you look physically deformed or extremely unattractive in a way that other people should also notice and be concerned about?

Um... yeah, I guess so. I mean, that's kind of why I made this appointment. I just... I can't stop focusing on it. 

Whenever I'm on video calls for work, or... looking at photos from my salsa class... the left side just looks so uneven and puffy to me. It looks really bad. But... everyone keeps telling me they don't see anything at all when I ask them. I don't know. It's just... it's starting to really mess with my work, and... my social life.
Have you ever looked in the mirror and felt that the left side of your face looked normal, or does it always seem like something is wrong with it, no matter how many times you check?
Um... I don't think so. It just... always looks wrong to me. I don't really remember a time recently where I looked and thought it was fine.
